newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica rice purchase tender suspended.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica rice purchase tender suspended.

text.p: Costa Rica suspended Monday the buy tender for 30,000 tonnes of rice because of high prices from the 16 companies that tendered, an official from Granos Basicos de Centroamerica said.

Alvaro Cordero, executive director of the private company in charge of the tender for the industrial rice sector, said they had decided to suspend the tender and re-open it in late April, looking for lower prices.
"We decided today that we are not going to buy for the moment and will wait 22 to 30 days to open a new tender, Cordero told Reuters.
Cordero explained that the buy tender, which was opened on March 12 and closed March 19, had resulted in offers of prices at least 13 percent over local prices.
"The minimum price that they offered us was $287.69 per tonne, against $271.00 for local Costa Rican prices," he added.
He said the tender attracted bids from U.S. and Argentine companies, although he did not name them.
Costa Rican rice industrialists held talks with the government over the weekend and the upshot was the decision to put back the tender to next month.
Cordero said Costa Rica bought 23,000 tonnes of rice in early in March. The shipment from New Orleans in the United States was priced at $288.00 per tonne, he said.
Also, he said the company has accepted a offer to buy 26,500 tonnes of rice from Argentina at $286.00 per tonne. That shipment is scheduled April 1, he added.
Costa Rica has forecast rice production at 185,000 this year compared to consumption levels at an anticipated 275,000 tonnes. The shortfall will be made up with imports.
